reviews.rationale: Selected-exhibit sequential review of the Q3 packet against the Q2 baseline. Supportive: GAAP net income, pretax income, net interest income after provision, net interest income, and total noninterest income all display higher values sequentially, and the credit-loss provision displays lower, so the earnings direction is favorable on the displayed GAAP subtotals. Opposing: the reported annualized net charge-off ratio and the company-defined ratio excluding acquisition-date effects both display higher, total ACL balance displays lower, ACL coverage of loans displays lower, and gross charge-offs display larger in magnitude, so the credit-quality trajectory is not uniformly improving even though the provision line fell. The non-GAAP adjusted net income and the after-tax merger-related component move in the same direction as their GAAP counterparts, so they do not provide independent corroboration. NPA totals and the NPA-to-assets ratio are essentially flat, and the non-acquired NPA line is marginally higher while acquired NPA is lower, which is consistent with a mixed rather than a clean improvement. Tax provision displays higher alongside higher pretax income, which is an expected same-direction relationship and not evidence of a smaller tax drag. All figures are selected displayed rows compared sequentially, not year-over-year, and no causal driver is established by the arithmetic. Because the credit-quality signals conflict with the earnings direction and the packet lacks loan-growth, reserve-build, and mix detail needed to reconcile them, the research state is held for review rather than advanced.
